messages:
sam: Heads-up — we're seeing ~7% of requests with service-account tokens routed to the cold GPU pool and billed to the wrong project. dashboard spike at 03:12 UTC. Anyone else seeing the origin attribution gap?

rachel: wow, that's bad. any obvious pattern (org vs project vs token prefix)?

liam: quick check: paging some logs now. pattern looks like ephemeral SA tokens from integration-workflows service. sometimes origin header missing.

sam: logs: ```INFO auth=ok token_kind=service_account origin_header= - routed_pool=cold-pool project=unknown cost_center=org-42```

mike: that `origin_header= -` is the kicker. means auth proxy didn't attach org-project. fallback logic currently sets project=null and routing picks default pool -> cold.

rachel: is this a quota or routing bug? could be auth proxy dropping header during impersonation dance.

liam: leaning auth-proxy. we added a header rewrite optimization last week to reduce headers for large batch calls. might be clobbering the X-Redwood-Origin header.

ops-bot: alert: routing-anomaly (service-account origin) threshold crossed (5m avg >5%). Incident channel pinged.

sam: immediate mitigations? we should avoid cross-project billing. options: 1) fail fast if origin missing, 2) default to org-billed pool (safer), 3) attach a temporary sticky-routing override based on token hash.

mike: prefer option 2 short-term (less breaking). option 1 would surface failures to customers. option 3 is risky without telemetry.

rachel: agree on option 2 for rollback window. but we need a fix path and telemetry to prove origin attachment restored.

liam: I'll revert the header rewrite on auth-proxy canary and re-run the canary traffic. Patch is tiny: remove header-trim step in proxy middleware.

sam: rollout plan: revert on prod canary (flag=auth-proxy.header-trim=false) -> monitor routing-origin-rate -> if <1% after 10m promote -> then backfill telemetry + patch tests.

mike: need dashboard metrics updated: auth.origin_present ratio + billing.attribution_rate by project. current dashboard only shows routing-errors and pool-latency.

rachel: created an item for telemetry: add `auth.origin_present` counter + `billing.attributed` tag for routed requests. also add a heatmap of token_prefix -> project mapping.

liam: I'm on the immediate revert. pushing change to canary now. ```curl -XPOST https://deploy.internal/api/deploy -d '{"service":"auth-proxy","flag":"header-trim","value":false}'```

canary-bot: deploy started: auth-proxy v2.4.7 -> canary (15% traffic). CI checks ok.

ops-bot: note: setting sampling for attribution telemetry to 100% for 5m to capture traces.

sam: post-canary checks (what to watch): auth.origin_present pct, pool.routed=cold-pool pct, billing.unattributed_count, 95p latency for auth-proxy.

mike: we should also add a console UX tiny banner in the Sa/key view that warns when origin attribution missing in last 24h. product+support can triage user reports.

rachel: I'll file console banner task and link to runbook. also add an automated pager if unattributed billing > $50 in 1h window.

liam: canary results: after 6m origin_present jumped from 92% -> 99.6%, cold-pool routing down to baseline. rolling to 50% now.

canary-bot: deploy progressed: canary -> 50% (no errors), next step 100% in 10m unless blocked.

sam: awesome. followups: (A) telemetry PR (mike/rachel) (B) auth-proxy unit for header-trim edgecases (liam) (C) console banner + runbook (rachel) (D) retrospective on default routing policy (sam).

mike: I'll open the telemetry PR after lunch. small note: we should consider a future change where routing uses token-claims fallback (expensive but deterministic) rather than silence leading to default pool.

rachel: thanks all. feel free to DM if you need quick approvals. :thumbsup:

liam: logging trace id for a sample request: `trace=0af4c8d3 auth=svcA token=sha256:...` — will paste in incident doc.

ops-bot: incident resolved (origin attribution restored). summary: auth-proxy header-trim revert fixed missing origin header; followups scheduled.
